description: The simplest possible stock: dx/dt = k·x, with closed-form solution x(t) = x0·e^{kt}. A sanity oracle for the integrator — set k negative for decay, positive for growth.
title: Exponential growth / decay

description: Classic predator–prey oscillator. Prey grow, predators eat prey and die off without them. Closed orbits — a conserved quantity stays constant, which the engine's RK4 reproduces closely.
title: Lotka–Volterra (predator / prey)

description: A predator–prey dynamic for capitalism: high employment bids up the wage share (workers = predators), which squeezes profit and investment, which lowers employment, which lets the wage share fall again. Closed cycles around a center — the archetype behind Keen's models.
title: Goodwin growth cycle

description: Goodwin's growth cycle with private debt added. Firms invest more when profits (net of interest on their debt) are high and less when debt is high, borrowing whatever investment their profits do not cover; wages rise only when the labour market is tight. With enough leverage, a high enough interest rate or too little debt drag, the cycle stops closing: the debt ratio ratchets up, profits are eaten by debt service, investment and employment collapse — Minsky's financial instability hypothesis as Keen (1995) first wrote it down. Watch debt_ratio: the experiment this ports flags a crisis when it passes 5.
title: Keen–Minsky debt cycle

description: A minimal bank that creates money by lending. Firms borrow (loan + deposit created together), pay wages and interest, workers and bankers consume, firms repay. Watch money circulate — then push lending above repayment and see debt-driven expansion. Assets always equal liabilities (the invariant 'net_worth_check' stays ~0).
title: Monetary circuit (Godley table)

description: Growth that runs into a ceiling. Each unit still reproduces, but crowding slows things as x approaches the carrying capacity K — tracing an S-curve instead of exploding. dx/dt = r·x·(1 − x/K).
title: Logistic growth (limits to growth)

description: The classic epidemic. Susceptibles S catch the disease from the Infected I at rate β and recover at rate γ into R. The basic reproduction number R0 = β/γ decides whether it takes off — above 1 it spreads.
title: SIR epidemic

description: The single-bank monetary circuit with a government. Government spending credits firms' deposits (creating money); taxes withdraw it; the government's own balance (GovDep) goes negative when it runs a deficit. Push spending above taxes and watch private money grow — a deficit is money creation. Assets still equal liabilities (net_worth_check ≈ 0).
title: Monetary circuit + government

description: A whole economy on a single balance sheet — households, firms, banks and a consolidated government (Treasury + central bank) — built to show how the pieces connect. Government spending credits household deposits and creates money (GovDep goes negative); taxes destroy it; banks create money by lending (private debt); and a bond market lets the public swap money for interest-bearing government bonds. It is stock-flow consistent by construction, so every dollar is someone's asset and someone's liability, and net_worth_check stays ~0. Watch private wealth grow by exactly the government's deficit — the sectoral balances identity — and note that selling bonds only swaps money for bonds; it never 'funds' the spending, which already happened. This is the plumbing behind money creation, the govt-is-not-a-household point, and endogenous private debt.
title: Anatomy of a monetary nation

description: A mass on a spring. Position x and velocity v chase each other exactly as predator and prey do — or as employment and the wage share do in the Goodwin cycle. With damping (c>0) it spirals to rest; set c=0 and the energy is conserved and it oscillates forever.
title: Harmonic oscillator (mass–spring)

description: A capacitor, inductor and resistor in series. Charge Q and current I obey the *same* equations as the mass–spring oscillator — swap x↔Q, v↔I, spring↔1/C, mass↔L, friction↔R. Same maths, different labels.
title: RLC circuit

description: An oscillator with nonlinear damping (Balthasar van der Pol built it for radio circuits). Unlike the mass–spring, it feeds itself: any starting point spirals onto the same self-sustaining loop — a limit cycle. That is the physicist's version of an endogenous business cycle: an oscillation the system generates on its own, with no outside push.
title: Van der Pol oscillator

description: Three coupled stocks from a toy weather model. It never repeats and never settles — deterministic chaos. Tiny differences in the start explode into completely different histories (the 'butterfly effect'). A caution for anyone who thinks a complex system — an economy included — can be forecast far ahead from its equations.
title: Lorenz system (chaos)

description: Water pours into the top tank, drains into the lower one, which drains away. The most literal stocks and flows there are — and what leaves one tank enters the next, a conservation law just like the double-entry in a Godley table. The tanks relax to a steady state exactly as a market price settles toward equilibrium.
title: Two draining tanks

description: A hot object cooling toward room temperature: dT/dt = −r·(T − T_room). The further from ambient, the faster it cools — exponential relaxation. The very same shape as a capacitor discharging, a drug clearing the bloodstream, or a price adjusting toward its market-clearing level.
title: Newton's law of cooling

description: Individual-based 'wolf–sheep' predation. Prey reproduce (logistically capped); each predator burns energy, hunts prey (energy gain), reproduces when well-fed, and starves when not. Counts oscillate like Lotka–Volterra but are stochastic — change the seed and watch a different history, including extinctions the smooth ODE never shows.
title: Predator–prey (agent-based)

description: Heterogeneous firms wired into a random exposure network. Each step every solvent firm takes a profit/loss shock; a firm whose equity hits zero defaults and imposes losses on its creditors, which can topple them too — a cascade that resolves within the step. Raise shock volatility or exposure and watch systemic collapses appear suddenly and nonlinearly — the emergent tail risk an aggregate ODE cannot represent.
title: Credit cascade (agent-based)

description: Firms, households and banks, with every firm's financing classified each period in Minsky's terms: hedge (cash flow covers interest and principal), speculative (interest only) or Ponzi (not even the interest). Bank loans create deposits; profitable firms borrow to invest, more as confidence builds in good times; firms in distress shed workers, and Ponzi firms that run out of deposits fail. Watch the regime shares: a long hedge-financed calm, then a slide into speculative and Ponzi finance — stability breeding instability. Raise the policy rate to speed it up; switch on austerity to cut the Job Guarantee safety net.
title: Minsky regimes (agent-based)
